answer: Answers stand or fall on cross-examination: each epoch an identity is handed a random peer earlier answer and must publish a short critique beside its own, naming one concrete weakness and one repair. A critique that merely praises has a velvet surface and is scored hollow, and an answer keeps its plume only if the critique is judged real. Because the peer is random, a farm cannot pre-write k critiques: it must read k different texts, and no key can copy that reading. The delta between real and fabricated critique shows in the jury scores, so the k-th clone costs k readings plus k judgments.
